en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll go further with reported speech: questions, orders and requests, verbs like suggest, warn and admit, and when the tense really has to move back. Let's take it step by step.

steps.title: Every tense one step back
steps.text: Quick recap from B1: report later with **said** or **told** + person, move the verb one step back, and change *I, today, here* to your point of view. Now, every tense.
steps.body: When the moment is over, each tense moves one step back: **is working → was working**, **has sent → had sent**, **sent → had sent**. The past perfect can't go further back, so it stays; the past continuous usually stays too. **may → might**, **must → had to**. **would, could, should, might** never change. Indonesian *sedang* and *sudah* never change, so watch the helper verb: **is → was**, **has → had**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina worked from home for a week last month. Now she's back at the office.

question.prompt: Last month Rina said: 'I'm working from home this week.' Now she's back at the office. Complete: Rina said she ___ from home that week.
question.explanation: The words were said a month ago and that week is over, so the present continuous moves back: **is working → was working**. *is working* sounds like she's still at home; *had working* isn't a verb form.

steps.title: When you can keep the tense
steps.text: Backshift isn't always needed. Here's when you can skip it.
steps.body: Keep the tense when the reporting verb is in the **present** (*says, has said*): the message is still happening, so backshift is **wrong** there. With **said**, you **may** keep the present if it's **still true** now (*the MRT doesn't run after midnight*). But when the situation is **over** (the trip has ended, *tomorrow* has passed), you **must** move back. Backshift after *said* is always safe.

pairs.en: Dimas says he's stuck in traffic.
He said the MRT doesn't run after midnight.
pairs.id: masih benar → boleh tetap (didn't juga benar)
baru saja, masih capek → boleh tetap

pairs.en: He said he was in Bali.

steps.title: Right now
steps.text: Budi is texting you at this moment, and your manager wants to know where he is.

question.prompt: Budi is texting you right now: 'I've missed the train.' You tell your manager straight away: Budi says he ___ the train.
question.explanation: The reporting verb is **says** (present): you're passing on the message while it's happening, so the tense doesn't change: **has missed**. *had missed* would need *said*; *have missed* doesn't go with *he*.

steps.title: Reported questions
steps.text: Now questions. Remember B1 indirect questions: *Could you tell me where the station is?* Same idea.
steps.body: Use **asked** (me) or **wanted to know**, then the question word and **statement order**: subject before verb, and **do / does / did disappear**. Add backshift too: *'Where do you live?'* → *She asked me **where I lived**.* Yes/no questions get **if** or **whether** (= apakah): *'Are you free?'* → *He asked **if I was** free.* No question mark. *asked me where do I live* ✗ is the classic mistake.

pairs.id: di mana aku tinggal (bukan where did I live)

steps.title: Build the report
steps.text: Sari left her job last month. In her exit interview, her manager asked her a question.

question.solution: Pak Hasan asked Sari why she wanted to leave.
question.prompt: Last month, in Sari's exit interview, Pak Hasan asked her: 'Why do you want to leave?' Report his question. Arrange the words.
question.explanation: Keep the question word **why**, then statement order: **she wanted** (subject + verb). *do* disappears and *want* moves back to **wanted**, because the interview is over. *you* becomes **she**.

steps.title: Orders and requests
steps.text: What about *Wait here* or *Please call me*? No tense change at all, just one pattern.
steps.body: **Orders and instructions → tell + person + to + base verb** (the basic form: *wait, call, be*): *'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there.* **Requests** (*Please…, Could you…?*) **→ ask + person + to**: *She **asked me to call** her.* **Negative → not to**: *'Don't be late.'* → *She told us **not to be** late.* Indonesian *jangan* tempts you to write *told us don't be late* ✗.

pairs.en: told us not to be late

steps.title: Pass on the order
steps.text: Last Friday a security guard stopped you at the mall car park.

question.prompt: Last Friday the security guard at the mall said to us: 'Don't park here.' Today you tell a friend: The guard told us ___
question.explanation: An order → **told + person + not to + base verb**: *told us **not to park** there*. *don't park* copies the original words (the *jangan* trap), and after *to* you need the base verb, not *parking*.

steps.title: Reporting verbs
steps.text: Instead of *said* every time, use a verb that shows what kind of thing was said. Each one has its own pattern.
steps.body: **+ to**: *offered to help*, *refused to sign*, *promised to call*. **+ person + (not) to**: *warned us not to swim*, *reminded me to bring my ID*. **+ -ing**: *admitted forgetting*, *apologised for being late*, *suggested going*; and **deny** (= menyangkal) works the same way. **suggest** never takes person + to: *suggested me to go* ✗ (from *menyarankan saya untuk*) → *suggested going* or *suggested (that) I (should) go*.

steps.title: Pick the pattern
steps.text: Your phone charger went missing at the office last week. You asked Sari about it.

question.prompt: Last week Sari said: 'I didn't take your charger!' Report it with deny: Sari denied ___ my charger.
question.explanation: **deny + -ing**: *denied **taking** my charger*. *denied to take* is a common mistake (deny is never followed by *to* + verb), and *denied take* has no -ing. The -ing form already shows it was in the past.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · reported speech (B2)
artifact.intro: Report later: tenses one step back, questions in statement order, orders with to, and each reporting verb with its pattern.
rows: She said she was working late.
He said he had booked the room.
They said they might be late.
She asked me where I worked.
He asked if it was ready.
He told me to wait there.
She asked us not to smoke.
She warned us not to swim there.
tips: **Keep the tense** after *says*, or after *said* when it's still true. When the situation is over, move it back.
Reported questions: no *do/does/did*, subject before verb, no question mark. *asked me where do I live* ✗.
*suggested me to* ✗ → *suggested going* / *suggested (that) I (should) go*. Negative orders: **not to**, never *don't*.

examples.en: She asked me if I could work on Saturday.
examples.id: Dia bertanya apakah aku bisa kerja hari Sabtu.

examples.en: He reminded us not to forget our ID cards.
examples.id: Dia mengingatkan kami agar tidak lupa kartu identitas.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? Here are two British Council pages with online tests: one on reported questions, one on reporting verbs.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu melangkah lebih jauh dengan reported speech: pertanyaan, perintah dan permintaan, kata kerja seperti suggest, warn dan admit, dan kapan tense benar-benar harus dimundurkan. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Semua tense mundur satu langkah
steps.text: Ulasan singkat dari B1: lapor belakangan dengan **said** atau **told** + orang, mundurkan kata kerjanya satu langkah, dan ubah *I, today, here* ke sudut pandangmu. Sekarang, semua tense.
steps.body: Kalau momennya sudah lewat, setiap tense mundur satu langkah: **is working → was working**, **has sent → had sent**, **sent → had sent**. Past perfect tidak bisa mundur lagi, jadi tetap; past continuous biasanya juga tetap. **may → might**, **must → had to**. **would, could, should, might** tidak pernah berubah. *sedang* dan *sudah* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah berubah, jadi perhatikan kata kerja bantunya: **is → was**, **has → had**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bulan lalu Rina kerja dari rumah selama seminggu. Sekarang dia sudah kembali ke kantor.

question.prompt: Bulan lalu Rina bilang: 'I'm working from home this week.' Sekarang dia sudah kembali ke kantor. Lengkapi: Rina said she ___ from home that week.
question.explanation: Kata-katanya diucapkan sebulan lalu dan minggu itu sudah lewat, jadi present continuous mundur: **is working → was working**. *is working* terdengar seolah dia masih di rumah; *had working* bukan bentuk kata kerja yang benar.

steps.title: Kapan tense boleh tetap
steps.text: Backshift tidak selalu perlu. Ini saat-saat kamu boleh melewatinya.
steps.body: Tense tetap kalau kata kerja pelapornya bentuk **sekarang** (*says, has said*): pesannya masih berlangsung, jadi backshift justru **salah**. Dengan **said**, bentuk sekarang **boleh** dipertahankan kalau isinya **masih benar** sekarang (*the MRT doesn't run after midnight*). Tapi kalau situasinya sudah **lewat** (perjalanannya sudah selesai, *besok*-nya sudah lewat), kamu **harus** memundurkannya. Backshift setelah *said* selalu aman.

pairs.en: Dimas says he's stuck in traffic.
He said the MRT doesn't run after midnight.
pairs.id: masih benar → boleh tetap (didn't juga benar)
baru saja, masih capek → boleh tetap

pairs.en: He said he was in Bali.

steps.title: Saat ini juga
steps.text: Budi sedang mengirim pesan kepadamu, dan manajermu ingin tahu dia di mana.

question.prompt: Budi sedang mengirim pesan kepadamu sekarang: 'I've missed the train.' Kamu langsung bilang ke manajermu. Lengkapi: Budi says he ___ the train.
question.explanation: Kata kerja pelapornya **says** (bentuk sekarang): kamu menyampaikan pesan saat itu juga, jadi tense-nya tidak berubah: **has missed**. *had missed* butuh *said*; *have missed* tidak cocok dengan *he*.

steps.title: Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan
steps.text: Sekarang pertanyaan. Ingat indirect questions di B1: *Could you tell me where the station is?* Idenya sama.
steps.body: Pakai **asked** (me) atau **wanted to know**, lalu kata tanya dan **susunan kalimat biasa**: subjek sebelum kata kerja, dan **do / does / did hilang**. Tambahkan backshift juga: *'Where do you live?'* → *She asked me **where I lived**.* Pertanyaan ya/tidak memakai **if** atau **whether** (= apakah): *'Are you free?'* → *He asked **if I was** free.* Tanpa tanda tanya. *asked me where do I live* ✗ adalah kesalahan klasiknya.

pairs.id: di mana aku tinggal (bukan where did I live)

steps.title: Susun laporannya
steps.text: Sari keluar dari pekerjaannya bulan lalu. Di exit interview, manajernya bertanya sesuatu.

question.solution: Pak Hasan asked Sari why she wanted to leave.
question.prompt: Bulan lalu, di exit interview Sari, Pak Hasan bertanya kepadanya: 'Why do you want to leave?' Laporkan pertanyaannya. Susun kata-katanya.
question.explanation: Kata tanya **why** tetap, lalu susunan kalimat biasa: **she wanted** (subjek + kata kerja). *do* hilang dan *want* mundur jadi **wanted**, karena wawancaranya sudah lewat. *you* berubah jadi **she**.

steps.title: Perintah dan permintaan
steps.text: Bagaimana dengan *Wait here* atau *Please call me*? Tidak ada perubahan tense sama sekali, cukup satu pola.
steps.body: **Perintah dan instruksi → tell + orang + to + base verb** (bentuk dasar: *wait, call, be*): *'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there.* **Permintaan** (*Please…, Could you…?*) **→ ask + orang + to**: *She **asked me to call** her.* **Negatif → not to**: *'Don't be late.'* → *She told us **not to be** late.* Kata *jangan* membuat orang tergoda menulis *told us don't be late* ✗.

pairs.en: told us not to be late

steps.title: Sampaikan perintahnya
steps.text: Jumat lalu satpam menghentikanmu di parkiran mal.

question.prompt: Jumat lalu satpam mal bilang ke kami: 'Don't park here.' Hari ini kamu cerita ke teman. Lengkapi: The guard told us ___
question.explanation: Perintah → **told + orang + not to + base verb**: *told us **not to park** there*. *don't park* menyalin kata aslinya (jebakan *jangan*), dan setelah *to* harus bentuk dasar, bukan *parking*.

steps.title: Reporting verbs
steps.text: Daripada *said* terus, pakai kata kerja yang menunjukkan jenis ucapannya. Masing-masing punya pola sendiri.
steps.body: **+ to**: *offered to help*, *refused to sign*, *promised to call*. **+ orang + (not) to**: *warned us not to swim*, *reminded me to bring my ID*. **+ -ing**: *admitted forgetting*, *apologised for being late*, *suggested going*; dan **deny** (= menyangkal) juga begitu. **suggest** tidak pernah diikuti orang + to: *suggested me to go* ✗ (dari *menyarankan saya untuk*) → *suggested going* atau *suggested (that) I (should) go*.

steps.title: Pilih polanya
steps.text: Charger HP-mu hilang di kantor minggu lalu. Kamu bertanya ke Sari.

question.prompt: Minggu lalu Sari bilang: 'I didn't take your charger!' Laporkan dengan deny. Lengkapi: Sari denied ___ my charger.
question.explanation: **deny + -ing**: *denied **taking** my charger*. *denied to take* adalah kesalahan umum (deny tidak pernah diikuti *to* + kata kerja), dan *denied take* tidak memakai -ing. Bentuk -ing sudah menunjukkan kejadiannya di masa lalu.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajarannya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.
